source.title: Scaling Laws for Robust Comparison of Open Foundation Language-Vision Models and Datasets
source.authors: Marianna Nezhurina; Tomer Porian; Giovanni Puccetti; Tommie Kerssies; R. Beaumont; M. Cherti; J. Jitsev

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendix are present. The manuscript identifies itself as a preprint under review.
record.tranche_reason: The study derives and validates scaling laws for open language-vision models, extending scaling-law analysis to another modality and to downstream task errors rather than language-model pretraining cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The study measures downstream error rates and compute-optimal dataset sizes for CLIP, MaMMUT, and other vision-language systems. It does not measure held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy or a language-model parameter/token compute-optimal split. Rows for comparisons and fit behavior are included; cited results from other work are not treated as study results.
record.test_reason: The study fits saturating power laws in compute to downstream error for CLIP and MaMMUT image-text models across three datasets, two schedules and several tasks. It checks the fits against held-out larger runs, which bears on V5, V6 and V7 in a non-text-only setting. It measures no language-model pretraining cross-entropy or LM parameter/token split.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the following: the authors find the MaMMUT-over-CLIP crossover consistently between 1e10 and 1e11 GFLOPs across datasets, tasks and schedules. DFN-1.4B is best across tasks, while DataComp vs Re-LAION is task-dependent. A constant-LR derivation gives the same comparison at about 98% less compute. Repetition at 12.8B kept openMaMMUT-L/14 at 80.3%, below the predicted 82%.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses openCLIP/MaMMUT language-vision training and fits downstream error as a function of compute and samples seen. It does not reproduce the original language-model held-out cross-entropy measurement or the original language-model compute-optimal allocation method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports differences in fitted exponents across learning-rate schedules, dataset-dependent and task-dependent scaling comparisons, fit sensitivity to threshold and functional form, and diminished performance under high data repetition. It reports that the broad CLIP-versus-MaMMUT trend persists across cosine and constant schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: The ranking from scaling-law-based comparison is stable. MaMMUT overtakes CLIP between 1e10 and 1e11 GFLOPs across datasets, zero-shot tasks and LR schedules; DFN beats the other datasets; SigLIP shows no benefit over CLIP.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and dataset rankings derived from fitted scaling laws are robust to schedule, dataset and downstream task, although individual exponents vary.

record.peer_reviewed: Neural Information Processing Systems (venue as provided; manuscript text says preprint, under review)
record.problems: The study does not measure language-model pretraining cross-entropy. DataComp-1.4B and the other datasets limit low-repetition extrapolation to larger sample counts; DFN has fewer measurements and higher trend uncertainty. The cosine schedule uses a single run per model-samples-seen pair. The paper notes high uncertainty for some large-scale architecture extrapolations.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The paper reports many additional individual dataset/task fits and predictions in figures and appendices; these are not itemized separately here where they repeat the stated scaling trends.

untested.parts: All of it: held-out LM pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute.
All of it for LM pretraining loss. Held-out extrapolation here covers VLM downstream accuracy only, about 2–5x beyond the fit threshold.
All of it. Only a VLM Dopt(C)∝C^0.74 is fitted; there is no parameter/token split comparable to Kaplan or Chinchilla.
All of it. Shape at fixed parameter count is not varied as a controlled comparison.
Image-only and video models; scaling laws fitted under repeated data; LM fine-tuning or transfer.
Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss; language-model downstream tasks.

missing.what: Held-out predictions with the smaller fit threshold (2.5e11 GFLOPs). CLIP L-16 0.747 (0.738–0.755) vs 0.761; CLIP L-14 0.753 (0.744–0.762) vs 0.766; MaMMUT L-14@3B 0.773 (0.765–0.781) vs 0.784. All measured values lie above the CI. Also CLIP predictions with more points.
No-irreducible-error form over-predicts held-out accuracy, e.g. MaMMUT H-14 0.825 predicted vs 0.794 measured
CLIP ViT-L-14 12.8B prediction 0.796 (0.788–0.804) vs 79.2% reported by DataComp, within the CI. The measurement is external.
Constant-LR MS-COCO retrieval fits (CLIP αc -0.123 vs cosine -0.230; MaMMUT -0.335 vs -0.263)
Scaling-law fits for SigLIP, CoCa and Cap. CoCa extrapolation is highly uncertain.
Predicted Dopt and accuracy at unseen compute budgets

record.verdict_notes: The study measures downstream error of image-text models, not LM loss, so it bears only on V5, V6 and V7. The fitted form is a saturating power law with offset and irreducible-error terms. The paper itself notes that exponents alone do not rank scalability. Held-out extrapolation spans only about 2–5x in compute. R13 was wrongly listed under the V6 label in the reader's record; it is removed. The reader's V7 limits_scope label on R9 is dropped because repetition is not a fitting choice. The cosine schedule uses a single run per model and samples-seen pair.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy as a function of parameter count, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolation of language-model pretraining loss to much larger language-model runs. The paper validates predictions for vision-language downstream task errors instead.
The language-model parameter and token allocation at fixed compute, including the relative growth of language-model parameters and tokens.
The effect of depth, width, and other architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
The study tests language-vision models, including segmentation fine-tuning, but not image-only or video models, language-model repeated-data scaling laws, or language-model fine-tuning and transfer.
The study tests downstream task performance against compute, not a general relationship between downstream performance and language-model pretraining loss.
Fit and setup sensitivity is examined for vision-language models; the study does not establish whether language-model exponents or language-model compute-optimal allocations vary in the same way.

rows.subject: openCLIP and openMaMMUT (both)
rows.stage_stated: pre-trained on DataComp-1.4B, Re-LAION-1.4B, and DFN-1.4B
rows.operation_detail: Compare compute-dependent downstream error scaling across datasets and tasks.

conditions.value: ImageNet-1k zero-shot classification and MS-COCO retrieval

rows.measure: Relative downstream error across compute scales
rows.value: The paper reports DFN-1.4B as stronger across scales for both architectures and both tasks; DataComp has stronger classification scalability than Re-LAION, while retrieval is similar or slightly more favorable to Re-LAION.
rows.uncertainty: The authors note higher uncertainty for DFN trends because it has fewer measurements.
rows.note: This records the authors' stated dataset-level scaling comparisons, not individual plotted measurements.

rows.subject: openCLIP and openMaMMUT (both)

rows.operation_detail: Fit compute-dependent scaling laws to downstream segmentation error after fine-tuning.
rows.value: openMaMMUT exponent -0.354; error crossover at approximately 1e9 GFLOPs
rows.note: The authors state that MaMMUT scales more strongly for this fine-tuned downstream task; crossover is earlier than for zero-shot ImageNet classification.

rows.subject: openCLIP and openMaMMUT (both)

conditions.value: DataComp evaluation suite average over 35 tasks; ImageNet-V2; ImageNet robustness set

relationships.condition: CLIP/MaMMUT on DataComp, Re-LAION and DFN (1.4B unique samples, ≤3B samples seen). Covers zero-shot classification, retrieval, the 35-task suite, robustness and fine-tuned ADE20K.
relationships.reason: A saturating power law in compute fits downstream error across ~5 orders of compute, and Dopt follows a power law in C (R1–R6, R8, R13–R15).
relationships.display_finding: Saturating power laws fit downstream error across about five orders of compute, and optimal data size also follows a compute power law.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: CLIP/MaMMUT on DataComp, Re-LAION and DFN (1.4B unique samples, ≤3B samples seen). Covers zero-shot classification, retrieval, the 35-task suite, robustness and fine-tuned ADE20K.
source_check.reason: Sections 3.1–3.5 fit saturating power laws to language-vision downstream error, including segmentation after fine-tuning. The additional 35-task, robustness and segmentation evaluations use DataComp; DFN measurements extend only to 300M samples seen.

relationships.condition: Heavy data repetition (~9x, 12.8B samples on 1.4B unique)
relationships.reason: The unique-data law over-predicts: 0.803 measured vs 0.820 predicted, outside the CI. The authors attribute this to repetition (R9).
relationships.display_finding: Measured performance was 0.803 versus 0.820 predicted, outside the confidence interval, which the authors attributed to approximately ninefold data repetition.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Heavy data repetition (~9x, 12.8B samples on 1.4B unique)
source_check.reason: R9 compares one heavily repeated-data run with a prediction explicitly conditional on unique or low-repetition data. Its shortfall establishes a transfer limitation for that prediction, but does not test whether a power-law form holds across scales under heavy repetition.

relationships.condition: Held-out 3B-sample runs with the larger fit threshold (5e11 GFLOPs), low repetition
relationships.reason: MaMMUT H-14 0.795 lies within the CI (0.793–0.809) and L-14 0.784 is within 0.007 of its prediction. Downstream error scales smoothly across tasks (R7, R8, R14, R15).
relationships.display_finding: MaMMUT H-14 scored 0.795 within the predicted confidence interval of 0.793–0.809, while L-14 scored 0.784 within 0.007 of its prediction.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Held-out 3B-sample runs with the larger fit threshold (5e11 GFLOPs), low repetition
source_check.reason: Appendix C reports close held-out predictions: MaMMUT L-14 is 0.784 versus 0.777 predicted, while H-14 is within its 0.793–0.809 interval. L-14 slightly exceeds its interval, so this supports approximate predictability rather than universal interval coverage.

relationships.condition: High repetition; also fits with the smaller threshold (2.5e11 GFLOPs), per text Table 8
relationships.reason: R9 falls below its prediction. Per the Table 8 text (no row), several measured values exceed the narrow CIs, e.g. CLIP L-16 0.761 vs (0.738, 0.755).
relationships.display_finding: High repetition underperformed its prediction, while several measurements exceeded predicted intervals, including CLIP L-16 at 0.761 versus an interval of 0.738–0.755.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: High repetition; also fits with the smaller threshold (2.5e11 GFLOPs), per text Table 8
source_check.reason: Table 8 shows imperfect extrapolation with the smaller fit threshold, including CLIP L-16 at 0.761 versus a 0.738–0.755 interval. R9 additionally shows that low-repetition predictions require qualification before application to heavily repeated data.

relationships.condition: Schedule, functional form and dataset choices in VLM scaling fits on DataComp/Re-LAION/DFN
relationships.reason: Switching from cosine to constant LR shifts exponents (CLIP 0.227→0.168; MaMMUT 0.233→0.379). Dropping Ec raises held-out RMSE. Exponents differ by dataset (R10–R13).
relationships.display_finding: Switching from cosine decay to constant learning rate changed the CLIP exponent from 0.227 to 0.168 and MaMMUT's from 0.233 to 0.379; exponents also differed by dataset, and omitting Ec increased held-out RMSE.
